title: Советы бежать из города  (Advice to Flee the City)

segments.t: After Vika scolds Nastya for bringing the turtle back into the restaurant, the cooks return the pooled rubles because nobody can possibly raise a hundred thousand dollars by evening. Fedya and Senya seriously advise poor Lyova to pack his bags and flee town while he still can.
Настя, что Пашка здесь делает?
Ну, то я его с собой принесла.
Ну, мало ли что дома может случиться.
Настя, подойди сюда.
Так, все, мне идти надо.
Присмотри за ним.
Нет, ну, до вечера найти сто тысяч долларов...
Бежать тебе надо.
Не знаю, куда-нибудь.
Только ты мне адрес не говори.
Нет, ребят, куда бежать?
У тебя же нет детей.
Слушай, да расслабься ты.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Настя, что Пашка здесь делает?
'Nastya, what is Pashka doing here?' The grammar packs 'Nastya' and 'does' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ну, то я его с собой принесла.
'Well, I brought him along with me.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'then' in a few short words.
Ну, мало ли что дома может случиться.
'You never know what could happen at home.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'to happen' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
Настя, подойди сюда.
'Nastya, come over here.' Notice how Russian expresses 'Nastya' and 'here' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Так, все, мне идти надо.
'All right, that is it, I have to go.' Nastya anchors the line on 'like this', while 'at' completes the thought.
Присмотри за ним.
'Keep an eye on him.' In Russian, the idea of 'supervision' flows naturally into 'him' without extra filler words. Nastya answers right away.
Нет, ну, до вечера найти сто тысяч долларов...
'No way, finding a hundred thousand dollars before tonight...' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'there is no' before landing on 'dollars'.
Бежать тебе надо.
'You need to run away.' Vika anchors the line on 'to run', while 'at' completes the thought.
Не знаю, куда-нибудь.
'I do not know, somewhere far away.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'know' to negate the statement. Vika answers right away.
Только ты мне адрес не говори.
'Just do not tell me the address.' The grammar packs 'only' and 'say' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Нет, ребят, куда бежать?
'No, guys, where could I possibly run?' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'there is no' and 'kids' in a few short words.
У тебя же нет детей.
'You do not have any kids, at least.' In Russian, the idea of 'by' flows naturally into 'children' without extra filler words. Nastya answers right away.
Слушай, да расслабься ты.
'Listen, just relax.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'listen' before landing on 'you'. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.

Слушай, да расслабься ты.
